refentry.refsect1:
&reftitle.parameters;
socket
A Socket instance created with socket_create, socket_accept or socket_create_pair.
message
An array, passed by reference, which describes the buffers to prepare. It may contain the following elements:
name
An array, which may be empty. Only its optional family key is read: it selects the address family used to receive the address of the sender, which defaults to the family of socket. Without this element, the name element of the result is &null;.
buffer_size
The size in bytes of the buffer that receives the data, up to 104857600. It defaults to 8192. A message longer than the buffer is truncated.
controllen
The size in bytes of the buffer that receives the ancillary data. This element is required, and must be greater than 0. socket_cmsg_space computes the size needed for a given ancillary message.
On success, message is replaced by an array with exactly the keys described in the return values section, so the array cannot be reused as it is for another call. On failure it is left unchanged.
flags
A combination of the MSG_* flags of recvmsg(), joined with the binary OR (|) operator, for example MSG_PEEK, MSG_DONTWAIT, MSG_WAITALL, MSG_TRUNC or MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC. They depend on the platform. With MSG_TRUNC, the return value is the real length of a datagram, even when it is longer than the buffer.

&reftitle.returnvalues;
Returns the number of bytes received, or &false; on failure, in which case an E_WARNING is emitted. On success, message is an array with the following keys:
name
The address of the sender, as an array (family, addr and port for AF_INET), or &null; if the name element was not given.
control
The list of ancillary data messages received, each an array with the keys level, type and data. The supported messages are IPV6_PKTINFO, IPV6_HOPLIMIT, IPV6_TCLASS, SCM_CREDENTIALS and SCM_RIGHTS, whose file descriptors are received as Socket instances or stream resources.
iov
A list with one string: the data received.
flags
The flags of the received message, for example MSG_TRUNC when the data was truncated and MSG_CTRUNC when the ancillary data was.

&reftitle.errors;
A ValueError is thrown if flags is outside the range of an int. An Error is thrown if socket has already been closed.
